Welcome—it’s so good to have you here with me. Imagine this: you’re driving down a lonely highway, passing through towns that never make it onto postcards, catching glimpses of the real heart of a country most people never see. That’s the kind of journey we’re about to take together, inspired by Bill Bryson’s The Lost Continent. As we explore these forgotten places and overlooked highways, we’ll uncover the quirks, contradictions, and quiet charms that make small-town America so fascinating. Ever wondered what nostalgia really feels like when it bumps up against reality? Or what it’s like to search for a true sense of home in a world that keeps on changing? That’s exactly what we’ll be delving into—one winding road and faded main street at a time.
We’ll meet unforgettable locals, stumble across odd little roadside treasures, and soak in the beauty of the everyday. Each stop along the way isn’t just a new location—it’s a window into the soul of a country shaped by its memories and a future that’s still unwritten. Thanks to Bryson’s sharp wit and eye for the unexpected, this trip becomes so much more than just a travel story. It’s a personal quest, sure, but also a gentle, often humorous look at what it means to search for meaning in places that feel both familiar and totally new.
So, if you’re ready for a road trip that promises laughter, reflection, and maybe a little bit of longing, let’s get started. Together, we’ll discover what really makes America tick—one small town at a time.
